references.text: Jesus answers the Greeks' desire to meet him by proclaiming that his death is necessary so that the seed may bear much fruit, directly linking their presence to the expansion of salvation to all nations.
Jesus explains that when he is lifted up, he will draw all people to himself, fulfilling the search of the Greeks (representatives of the non-Jewish nations) for him.
The Jews wonder whether Jesus will go to the scattered Greeks to teach them, showing that the presence of Greeks in Jerusalem was a known phenomenon connected with messianic expectations.
Before the Greeks arrive, the Pharisees note that the whole world has gone after Jesus, placing their arrival in the context of a global movement toward him.
